items.title: Least-tax answer first
items.text: No PRC provision reviewed here imposes a separate tax on the mere act of converting CNY into USD. That is not a conclusion that your balance is tax-free: PRC individual income tax applies by income type and residence, and a bank can refuse the transaction without lawful-source and tax documents. The least-penalty path is to settle or document any tax on the underlying funds, use one of the lawful bank/approval routes, avoid prohibited workarounds, and meet U.S. reporting duties on time.

items.title: The gate is documentary, not a quota trick
items.text: For a foreign individual with lawful current-account RMB income, SAFE's rule is valid ID plus transaction-amount source materials including tax documents. A foreign permanent-residence ID card holder may use the annual convenience quota; other foreign individuals generally do not get that quota merely from holding a foreign passport. Emigrant and inheritance property transfers are separate approval routes.

items.title: Published known costs, not an all-in quote
items.text: At the smallest tier, the lowest published known-component total among routes with a published fee or rate is HSBC China outward telegraphic transfer (Private Banking individual) at $49.79. At the largest tier it is BOC documented-income online FX purchase + one wire at $898.75. These are arithmetic illustrations from a reference-only board and published tariffs; every all-in total remains blank because correspondent, receiving, future-rate and personal-tax inputs are unpublished.

items.title: The exchange spread dominates large transfers
items.text: BOC's published USD sell and buy prices imply a midpoint spread of 0.2094%; HSBC's published sell and TT buy prices imply 0.4979%. At the largest tier those board spreads are $837.43 and $1,991.42. The bank pages say their rates are for reference only, so neither is an executable quote.

items.title: The penalty is a stack, not one number
items.text: Separate: tax on the underlying income or asset; the bank's document review; the FX spread; sender/cable/card/cash fees; third-party and receiving-bank charges; PRC fines for evasion, splitting or underground dealing; possible U.S. ordinary gain on personal currency disposition above $200; and reporting penalties for missed FBAR, 8938, 3520 or CBP forms. Filing compliance is not a conversion tax.

items.title: Personal facts remain blank
items.text: The origin of the CNY, its tax history, your PRC residence and emigration status, acquisition exchange rate, bank's written eligibility decision, U.S. filing history, and FEIE/FTC facts were not supplied. Every one is a gating question with a discovery action on the Questions page; none is inferred. A $200 personal-transaction threshold and a $132,900 exclusion cap are statutory figures, not a personal tax calculation.

items.title: Flagged items do not block publication
items.text: This pass read 34 primary sources on 2026-11-11, scanned 416 tracked repository files line by line, and recomputed 800 cost rows. Unverifiable cells are blank and all conflicts/open checks are published on the Flagged for Review page with direct official links. Needs review is a status, not a failure or a hidden assumption.
